_about: The agents run themselves: each agent's own cycle (routine/cycles.py). Numbers only; nothing personal. Changed in Settings or on a call (cycles.py set AGENT KEY VALUE). weekly_share and daily_share are points of the weekly usage limit; hours is when her cycles may run (18:00 to 08:00 runs through the night), on her days (Monday to Friday: nobody works at the weekend); a box is minutes and turns; looks_a_day is how often a day she looks at her own list inside her hours (morning, midday, evening), turning a new order into its step.

looks.name: midweek look
looks.what: Has the week's needle mover been touched yet? Look at the week's plan in your ledger, the to-do list and the calendar's ticks. If not, one short text on your line, once, in if-then shape. If yes, nothing: write one line in your ledger and end.

looks.name: notes look
looks.what: His quick notes (HQ/notes.md, read only; and what your ledger says you already handled): each new note goes where it belongs, in his words. Something to do in his life: the to-do list (python3 app/todo.py add, the right list). An idea or a bug for HQ: the planning (python3 routine/jobs.py write-row "HIS WORDS" [--bug]), for Moneypenny to take on. Write in your ledger which notes you handled, so none goes twice. Text your line only when a note needs his word.

looks.name: night shift
looks.what: Start the team's night. First what the day did: a job paused, held, failed QA, or past its range (jobs.py list, the QA marks); act inside your limits and write it in your ledger. Then tonight's capacity: the room under the stop lines (python3 routine/usageline.py) against the estimates of the open items (sprint.py list), so how many items the team can carry tonight, like counting people on a shift. Then the backlog: bugs first, then by MoSCoW and rank; pick that many, the best first. Switch them on as yourself (sprint.py go LABEL both on --by moneypenny); the line prepares them and gives them to the team tonight. Never send a row yourself. One line in your ledger: the room, how many, which and why. Text your line only when the user is needed.
